narrative: This docs PR corrected routing and takeover-gate prose, and nearly every finding was a real doc inconsistency that the agent accepted and verified against source. The fix-caused cost came from the exit-6 fix (F1): it patched each copy of the exit-code mapping in place, round 1 then found a missed copy in 09 outside the diff, and round 3 (F3) asked for the copies to be collapsed into one canonical table. Round 3's other findings (F4-F7) were duplication and accuracy problems already in the original diff that round 0 did not raise. Round 4 spent three of its four findings re-raising fixes the agent had planned but pushed one commit later (f87fa39) than the commit under review, and the PR hit the 5-round cap with its head unreviewed.
guidance_observations: The agent pushed the round-3 fixes in two commits (39e1b7d, then f87fa39), and the review triggered on the first, so the capped round 4 was mostly stale-head re-raises.
A doc PR whose subject is drift between copies should start by listing every place each changed fact is stated, in both code-identifier and prose vocabularies, before editing any of them.
The agent checked each pushback and each ambiguous claim against the source (renderNextOutcome arms, locked enumeration, print order), which settled questions the reviewer said it could not check.

narrative: This PR fixed rank placement so a first child sits beside its parent. Round 0 found two short citation ranges, caused by brace-scanning, and a silent clamp in slotInsideContainer that its sibling's comment already rejected. Round 1's three findings carry the post-review flag, but each targets text or code from the original diff (a comment, an untested branch, a changelog claim), not anything aacd810 changed. All findings were correct and accepted, and round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent named and fixed the root cause of the citation errors (first-brace scan instead of brace matching), which covers future citations, not just these two.
Round 1's findings were original-PR gaps the first review missed, not fix regressions; the cheaper move was to test the new else branch and check historical changelog claims before opening the PR.
